solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Step on board cool craft for a long journey

indicators.note: on board is the crossword way of saying inside a ship, so the step goes into the ship's letters

parts.note: a ship is boarded; SS stands for steamship
a pace is a step
hip means cool or fashionable

explanation.surface: An invitation to step aboard a trendy vessel for a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a standing convention: whatever is on board sits between the two letters of the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle built for travel through outer space is a craft that makes very long journeys.

clue.text: Cover for bud, an elite US Navy man seizing power

indicators.note: seizing says the navy man's letters grab and hold the power letter

parts.note: a SEAL is a member of the US Navy's special forces

explanation.surface: A special-forces sailor seizes power while covering for his buddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bud' looks like a friend, as in buddy, but it is a flower bud.
explanation.definitionFit: The green leaf-like parts of a flower enclose and protect it before it opens.

clue.text: Air cut sugar till processed for farmer

indicators.note: processed says the letters of the four words are treated and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A grower's routine of airing and cutting sugar until it is processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who practises agriculture, working the land, is a farmer.

clue.text: Colour of European poet I loved at the outset

parts.note: W H Auden was a 20th-century poet

indicators.note: at the outset takes only the first letter of the preceding word

explanation.surface: A colour belonging to a European poet I adored from the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale greenish shade, French for Nile water.

clue.text: Military equipment needs right warhead fitting

indicators.note: fitting says the letters are being assembled and fitted together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Weapons need the correct warhead to be fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons, vehicles and other armaments are collectively the materiel of an army.

clue.text: Upset resin under power-assisted steering unit

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, places the resin below the steering letters

parts.note: PAS abbreviates power-assisted steering

indicators.note: Upset, in a down clue, means turned upside down so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lac is a resin secreted by insects

explanation.surface: Spilt resin under a car's steering assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses LAC to CAL, which goes under PAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI measure of pressure is named after Blaise Pascal.

clue.text: Avoids dear trousers of strong cotton

definitions.meaning: to duck a question or a blow is to avoid it
a northern English term of endearment, as in 'ta, love'
heavy cotton or linen trousers, as worn by sailors, are called by the name of that cloth

explanation.surface: Someone sidesteps a fine pair of heavy cotton trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition. 'Ducks' is a friendly form of address in parts of England, like 'love'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is a separate meaning of the same word: dodges, a pet name, and canvas trousers.

clue.text: Go further down river meeting swan laying eggs

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the Welsh border
a pen is a female swan, the one that lays eggs

explanation.surface: A river where a swan is nesting.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something deeper is to take it further downward.

clue.text: My lecturer's a fool to expose English as a block to communications

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!
a don is a university lecturer; don's gives DONS
a nit is a fool, nitwit
to air is to expose or make public

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the lecturer is a fool to expose English as a barrier to communication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive but the exclamation COR.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarded line cutting off an infected area, or a buffer zone, blocks movement and contact.

clue.text: Yield is less uncertain either side of break

indicators.note: either side of says the first word's letters lie on both sides of the breaking word

parts.note: surer means more certain, so less uncertain
to rend is to tear or break

explanation.surface: Giving in is less doubtful on either side of a rupture.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or give way is to yield.

clue.text: One chasing accounting officer around university

indicators.note: around says the officer's letters enclose the university letter

parts.note: a purser is the officer handling a ship's accounts

explanation.surface: A finance officer is chased round a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pursues is a person chasing after another.

clue.text: Artist turned into downright wool-gatherer

indicators.note: into says the turned artist goes inside the word for downright

parts.note: sheer means utter or downright, as in sheer nonsense

indicators.note: turned means the artist's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter becomes a total daydreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses RA to AR, which goes into SHEER. A wool-gatherer is usually a daydreamer; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep-clipper literally gathers fleece, making the idiom for an absent-minded person a playful definition.

clue.text: What's attractive about Conservative money?

indicators.note: about says the attractive thing goes round the Conservative's letter

parts.note: a lure is something that attracts or tempts

explanation.surface: A question about what draws people to Tory finances.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy lucre is a disparaging term for cash, especially gained dishonestly.

clue.text: How baleen is put in another way?

definitions.text: How baleen is put in another way?

indicators.note: put in another way says the letters of the preceding words are reworded into a new order

explanation.surface: A question asking for a synonym of the word baleen.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of HOW BALEEN give the answer, which is also literally baleen expressed in another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleen is the horny filter material in the mouths of certain whales, commonly called by this compound name.

clue.text: Dance with girl — one covered in fat

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: covered in says the numeral letter is wrapped by the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Dancing with a girl who is coated in grease.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Renaissance court dance in triple time, often paired with the pavane.

clue.text: Argue crazily about bet security

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the stake
crazily says the letters of the word argue are jumbled

parts.note: an ante is a stake or bet in poker

explanation.surface: People squabbling wildly over a betting deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazily' gives GUARE, and 'about' wraps those letters round the poker stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge or surety given as a promise is a form of security.

clue.text: Insulted when the sailor's gone and cast off

indicators.note: gone says the sailor's letters are removed

parts.note: abused means insulted
AB, able seaman, is the crossword sailor

explanation.surface: Someone was insulted once the sailor had left and been discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand clothing that has already been worn is cast off by its first owner.

clue.text: Purchase a lot of beer, always filling

indicators.note: filling says the word for always goes inside
a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: lager is a kind of beer
ever means always

explanation.surface: Buying a large quantity of beer, constantly topping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims LAGER to LAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a grip or hold giving mechanical advantage, the same as leverage.

clue.text: What's used to haul weight on rocky islands

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaken, so the letters of islands are scrambled

explanation.surface: A question about what hauls weights on rugged islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch with a horizontal drum on which a rope winds is a hauling device.

clue.text: Plant attached to a wall endlessly knocked about

indicators.note: knocked about says the letters are turned round, here back to front
endlessly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a mural is a painting on, or attached to, a wall

explanation.surface: A plant fixed to a wall that has been battered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts MURAL to MURA; 'knocked about' turns it round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The lily family includes this genus, cuckoo-pint or lords-and-ladies being a familiar species.

clue.text: One starting to solicit money inside

parts.note: to beg is to ask for money
inner means inside

explanation.surface: Someone who has just begun asking for cash from within.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is someone at the start of learning something.

clue.text: Urgently taking son round to bank

parts.note: O is round in shape
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: Desperately bringing a son around to the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorely needed means needed badly or urgently.

clue.text: Some grub is troughed here

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some food is wolfed down at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue suggests the place, with 'here' standing for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small restaurant is a place where food is eaten, so the definition points to it.

clue.text: Examine a military alliance one's come across in Middle East

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization

indicators.note: come across in says the second piece has been met inside the region's letters

parts.note: one's is I'S, with I for one

explanation.surface: Scrutinising an alliance that has encountered someone in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect or analyse something in minute detail is to examine it closely.

clue.text: First of inebriates getting dry in party — "same again"

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: First of says only the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry or not drinking

explanation.surface: A drunk turns teetotal at a party, then orders the same again.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is the word for repeating what was said before, the same once more.

clue.text: One living at their peak in old book

parts.note: a book is a read, as in a good read

explanation.surface: A mountain-dwelling figure found in an ancient volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At their peak' sounds like success, but means literally on a mountain top.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph of Greek myth who inhabits mountains lives on the peaks.

clue.text: Free energy in high explosive weapon

indicators.note: in says the freeing and energy letters go inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive
to rid is to free
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Releasing power from an explosive weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-pronged spear, and also the name of Britain's nuclear missile system.

clue.text: Key sin involving all rapacity, primarily

definitions.text: Key sin involving all rapacity, primarily

parts.note: A is a musical key

indicators.note: involving says the sin's letters enclose the picked initials

parts.note: a vice is a sin

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A cardinal sin, which is all about grasping greed.
explanation.walkthrough: A whole-clue reading: the wordplay builds the answer while the clue as a whole describes greed, one of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed for wealth is one of the seven deadly sins and amounts to complete rapacity.

clue.text: Privileged classes devoid of good record

indicators.note: devoid of says the good letter is removed

parts.note: the gentry are the upper or privileged classes

explanation.surface: The upper classes have no record of good behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: An item written in a ledger, diary or register is a record of something.

clue.text: Many balls finish without pressure to go beyond budget

indicators.note: without means outside, so the pressure letter sits outside the finishing word, before it

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls, so overs are many balls
P is the physics symbol for pressure
end means finish

explanation.surface: A cricket innings dragging on without strain until it overshoots its budget.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the game of bat and ball, an over is six balls bowled. 'Without' here means outside: P stands outside END.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend more than one can afford is to exceed a budget.
